data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 argues that decentralized networks are less resilient because operators react with similar 'panic' heuristics during systemic stress, creating a correlated human-error failure mode. This mechanism presumes that monolithic operators behave fundamentally differently—yet it provides no causal argument for why the centralized operators of a single large service would be immune to the same panic heuristics or would not also issue simultaneous restarts or identical config changes under systemic stress. Worse, in a monolith there is a single operational authority, so a single bad decision propagates by construction; the causal mechanism actually predicts *higher* human-error correlation in the monolith, not lower. SRC_001 thus fails to establish the key comparative causal link its claim depends on.
